title: Residual pseudodifferential operators have smooth distributional kernels
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Let $N$ be a compact oriented smooth manifold without boundary of dimension $m\geq1$, with a smooth Riemannian metric and its positive volume form $dV$. Let $E,F,G$ be smooth finite-rank real vector bundles. Use the distribution spaces, symbol classes $S^r$ and operator classes $\Psi^r$ of [def-sfb-symbol-pseudodifferential-operators]. Let $T:\mathcal D\prime(E)\to\mathcal D\prime(F)$ be a continuous real-linear map. If $T\in\Psi^{-L}(E,F)$ for every integer $L\geq1$, then there exists a real smooth section $$K\in\Gamma^\infty\bigl(N\times N,\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf R}(\operatorname{pr}_2^*E,\operatorname{pr}_1^*F)\bigr)$$ such that $T=R_K$ as maps on all of $\mathcal D\prime(E)$. Here $R_K$ is defined using $dV$ and distributional duality as in [def-sfb-symbol-pseudodifferential-operators]; on smooth sections, $$Tu(x)=\int_NK(x,y)u(y)\,dV(y).$$

source.place: Demailly, Part I §3.B, printed pp.12–14 (PDF pages 24–26); WANTED locally, read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/hodge-ams.pdf; paragraph following Proposition 3.6, printed p.13: regular operators and smooth integral kernels; residual-order formulation with equality of distributional actions.

proof.text: Fix $k\geq0$ and take $L=m+k+1$. The hypothesis and [def-sfb-symbol-pseudodifferential-operators] give a finite representation $T=\sum_i\chi_i\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Op}(a_i)\psi_i+R_{S_k}$ with each $a_i$ of order $-L<-m-k$ and $S_k$ smooth. Apply [lem-sfb-negative-symbol-finite-kernel] in each chart. Write $dV=\gamma_i(y)\,dy$ there, with $\gamma_i>0$. The real local matrix kernel $\operatorname{Re}H_i(x,y)/\gamma_i(y)$ defines a bundle homomorphism $E_y\to F_x$ in the chosen frames. Extend it by zero; its support lies in $\operatorname{supp}\chi_i\times\operatorname{supp}\psi_i$, a compact subset of the chart product, so this is a global $C^k$ section of the required Hom bundle. The finite sum with $S_k$ is a real $C^k$ kernel $K_k$. The local integral identity and the factor $\gamma_i^{-1}$ show, for every smooth section $u$, that $$Tu=\int_N K_k(\mathord\cdot,y)u(y)\,dV(y)$$ as distributions, with a continuous (indeed $C^k$) representative. This construction allows a different representation of $T$ for each $k$; it does not assume one symbol belongs to every negative order.

source.place: Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, §3, (3.3)–(3.5), Schwartz kernel (3.8)–(3.9), pp.6–8, and regularizing operators (3.12), pp.9–10. WANTED locally; read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/analytic_geometry_2019/pseudodiff.pdf. Finite differentiability version of the Fourier-kernel argument, with the 1/(2π)^m convention of def-sfb-symbol-pseudodifferential-operators.

proof.text: We will use the following consequence of the three cited scalar statements: a continuous bundle section representing the zero distribution is zero pointwise. In a chart and frame, test one coefficient against $g\,|dx|$ with arbitrary smooth real $g$ compactly supported in that chart. That coefficient, viewed as complex-valued and extended by zero off the chart, is locally integrable by [lem-sfb-continuous-local-integrability]. Its test integrals vanish, so [lem-sfb-smooth-test-ae-separation] makes it zero almost everywhere on the chart. By [lem-sfb-continuous-ae-pointwise] it is zero at every point of the chart. Apply this to every coefficient and every chart. The test-density and smooth-section embeddings used here are precisely [def-sfb-smooth-bundle-test-distributions]; no fibre metric or trivialization of the bundle globally is needed.

proof.text: For every smooth $u$, the continuous sections obtained in step 1 for $k$ and $0$ represent the same distribution $Tu$. Step 2 therefore gives $$\int_N (K_k-K_0)(x,y)u(y)\,dV(y)=0\quad\text{for every }x.$$ Fix $x$ and one coordinate functional on $F_x$. In any input chart and frame, take $u$ with one coefficient an arbitrary compactly supported smooth real function $g$ and all other coefficients zero, and extend it by zero. Each resulting scalar coefficient $h(y)$ of $(K_k-K_0)(x,y)$ is continuous. The displayed identity says $\int g(y)h(y)\gamma(y)\,dy=0$. By [lem-sfb-continuous-local-integrability], $h\gamma$ is locally integrable; [lem-sfb-smooth-test-ae-separation] and [lem-sfb-continuous-ae-pointwise] give $h\gamma=0$ pointwise. Since $\gamma>0$, $h=0$. All input coefficients and output coordinate functionals vanish in this way, hence $K_k=K_0$ pointwise on $N\times N$.

proof.text: Set $K=K_0$. For every finite $k$, step 3 identifies this very section with the $C^k$ section $K_k$. Thus every local matrix coefficient is $C^k$ for all $k$, which is the definition of smoothness. The kernel is real, has the required bundle type, and its integral agrees with $Tu$ on all smooth $u$ by step 1.

source.place: Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, §3, (3.3)–(3.5), Schwartz kernel (3.8)–(3.9), pp.6–8, and regularizing operators (3.12), pp.9–10. WANTED locally; read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/analytic_geometry_2019/pseudodiff.pdf. Finite differentiability version of the Fourier-kernel argument, with the 1/(2π)^m convention of def-sfb-symbol-pseudodifferential-operators.

proof.text: Use one finite representation of $T$, for example the one with $L=m+1$. By the transposition convention of [def-sfb-symbol-pseudodifferential-operators], it has a test-density transpose $B$ with $(Tu)(\phi)=u(B\phi)$ for every distribution $u$. Both spatial cutoffs are included in each local transpose. The same definition gives the transpose $C_K$ of the smooth-kernel action, with $(R_Ku)(\phi)=u(C_K\phi)$. Explicitly, if $\phi(x)=\ell(x)dV(x)$, then $$(C_K\phi)(y)=\left(\int_N\ell(x)\circ K(x,y)\,dV(x)\right)dV(y).$$ For every smooth $u$, step 4 gives $u(B\phi-C_K\phi)=((T-R_K)u)(\phi)=0$. The difference is a smooth dual-density section. Test its coefficients using arbitrary smooth $u$ supported in one chart. The scalar local-integrability, test-separation and continuous-almost-everywhere statements, exactly as in step 2, imply $B\phi-C_K\phi=0$ pointwise. Consequently $(Tu)(\phi)=u(B\phi)=u(C_K\phi)=(R_Ku)(\phi)$ for every $u\in\mathcal D'(E)$ and every test $\phi$. Equality of functionals proves $T=R_K$ on all distributions. No approximation of $u$ or Sobolev assumption is used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q95-94993e9bd (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new node lem-sfb-negative-symbol-finite-kernel and every cited statement in full: def-sfb-symbol-pseudodifferential-operators, def-sfb-smooth-bundle-test-distributions and the three scalar leaves (local integrability, smooth-test a.e. separation, continuous a.e.-to-pointwise). The source is Demailly (Hodge-AMS §3.B and the pseudodifferential course §3, (3.8)-(3.13)). Neither is in literature/ and both are marked WANTED, so I checked the mathematics directly, not against the source. New node: on supp χ, a mixed derivative of order ≤k of the integrand is bounded by C(1+|ξ|)^{r+k}, which is integrable because r<-m-k. Dominated convergence then gives C^k regularity, the derivative formulas and uniform convergence of the ρ(ξ/R) truncations. Fubini gives the action identity, and Re(Hf)=(Re H)f gives the real clause for real f. Support in supp χ × supp ψ, compact in U×U, makes the extension by zero C^k. The strict inequality is needed: at r=-m-k the integral diverges logarithmically. For m=1, k=0, r=-2 the kernel is continuous but not C^1, which fits the threshold. The node is a statement only, self-contained, strictly smaller than the item and not one of its clauses. It duplicates no existing node (compact-symbol-frequency-kernel and fourier-moment-representative differ), and its searches are logged. Step 1: L=m+k+1 gives order -L<-m-k. Dividing by γ_i converts dy to dV, the kernel has the direction E_y→F_x, and extension by zero gives a global C^k K_k. A different representation is allowed for each k. Steps 2-3: the three scalar leaves are applied with their hypotheses met. Continuous representatives agree pointwise, and testing against single-coefficient chart-supported u gives hγ=0, hence K_k=K_0 since γ>0. No Schwartz kernel theorem is used. Step 4 (elementary): K_0 is C^k for every k, so it is smooth. Step 5: the transposes of the definition give (Tu)(φ)=u(Bφ). Bφ-C_Kφ is a smooth dual density that every smooth u annihilates, so it is zero, and T=R_K on all distributions with no density or Sobolev argument. This matches how the citer, lem-sfb-elliptic-distribution-parametrix, uses the item in its step 4. No repair note applies, there is no SGA citation, the blueprint fields are consistent with the inherited null ancestor, there are no tool_uses and I made no changes.
